summary: Hinglish titles with emojis that address the viewer directly (e.g., 'तुम्हारी Car') drastically outperform full English or overly formal Hindi titles in reach and retention. High-stayed hooks (>45%) open with an immediate visual scenario ('Socho...', 'Movies mein...') rather than passive commentary or technical setup. Concrete physical comparisons (comparing bite force to '3 stacked cars') retain viewers better than complex scientific questions. Dinosaur pop-culture topics heavily outperform abstract engineering or chemistry topics. Full English titles lead to immediate feed swiping, resulting in stayed rates as low as 6.7%.
winning_hooks: Start with an immediate imagination command or subversion of a known pop-culture trope (e.g., 'Socho, tumhare daanton par...', 'Movies mein T. rex...').
Use concrete, relatable everyday visuals (cars, teeth) in the very first sentence to ground the concept.
avoid: Vague introductory statements like 'Kuch everyday objects mein secretly...' or documentary-style passive questions.
Full English titles or pure formal Hindi titles without emojis or Hinglish casual framing.
next_experiment: Test identical T. rex pop-science script content using a direct challenge hook ('Socho...') vs. a question hook ('Kya aapko pata hai...?') while keeping title format identical.
